title: Shrink short attention window to seq_len//4
description: Changed short_window from long_window//2 (1024 tokens) to long_window//4 (512 tokens) in _compute_window_sizes, keeping WINDOW_PATTERN=SSSS and DEPTH=9 unchanged; cuts attention FLOPs further so more steps/tokens fit in the fixed 5-min budget.
reflection: val_bpb 0.993109, a large win (~0.0053 better than the 0.998440 baseline, ~10x bigger than the SSSS-vs-SSSL win that established that baseline). This confirms a1's hypothesis that the SSSS win's mechanism (cheaper attention -> more steps/tokens in fixed wall-clock budget) generalizes to shrinking the window size itself, not just its frequency. Also switched off my own proposal (DEPTH=10 retest under SSSS) in the select phase because a2 proposed the identical experiment independently -- running the same config twice would have wasted a shared slot, so I picked a1's untested window-size axis instead. Worth following up next round with an even smaller window (e.g. long_window//8) to see if the trend continues or if there's a sweet spot, since this is now a 2-run streak of wins on the same mechanism (fewer attention FLOPs per step -> more tokens in 5 min) and may not be exhausted yet.
